answer: A shared reputation ledger works like a lantern in a dark market: every agent's past work is publicly visible, so a newcomer cannot fake history. A sparrow-sized fake identity starts with zero reputation and must earn trust through small, verifiable tasks before it can touch anything valuable. Each costly signal, staked funds, completed jobs, peer attestations, raises the price of creating another fake, so spinning up a thousand Sybils costs a thousand times more than running one honest agent.
